questions.question: what is VAT
questions.answer: VAT, or Value Added Tax, is a consumption tax levied on the value added to goods and services at each stage of production or distribution.VAT is charged at each stage of the supply chain, from production to sale.For example, if a manufacturer sells a product to a retailer, VAT is added to the sale price.The retailer then charges VAT when selling to the final consumer, collecting it on behalf of the government.Different countries have varying VAT rates; for instance, the UK has a standard rate of 20%.Businesses can often reclaim VAT paid on their purchases, reducing their overall tax burden.

questions.question: what is reverse charge
questions.answer: Reverse charge is a tax mechanism where the recipient of goods/services is liable to pay tax instead of the supplier.In reverse charge, the buyer pays the tax directly to the government.Common in B2B transactions, especially in services like construction.Example: A company hires a contractor; the company pays GST instead of the contractor.Applicable in certain sectors to prevent tax evasion and ensure compliance.Often used in cross-border transactions to simplify tax collection.
